title: Structured sunflowers and canonical Ramsey properties
summary: A first-order structure $M$ is said to have the infinite sunflower property if, for each $k \in \mathbb{N}_+$ and each structure $M' \cong M$ whose elements are $k$-sets, there is $S \subseteq M'$, $S \cong M$, such that $S$ is a sunflower: a collection of sets such that each pair of elements has the same intersection.
